text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali and Emir of Bahrain stress in talks in Manama the depth of Jordanian-Bahraini ties; the two sides discuss setting up a joint Bahraini-Jordanian bank to promote investments.
- Agriculture ministry proposes solutions to boost food production which include incentives for farmers to grow cereals and wheat.
- Transport minister again rejects Israel's technical and security conditions attached to an initialled agreement for joint use of Jordan's Aqaba airport.
- Crown Prince Hassan to visit Hungary next week to head a world gathering of orientalist researchers.
- The militant Palestinian Islamist movement Hamas reinstates Musa Abu Marzook, its former politburo head who was freed from U.S. jail, to its leadership structure, sources say.

- Jordan signs investment guarantee accord with the United States which will promote joint ventures and adds safeguards to U.S. investors. Jordan to sign this month an accord with Washington to grant it an extra $100 million of aid in 1997.
- Prime Minister Majali's popularity drops slightly after 100 days in government - poll.
